view.summary: Goldman kept the Brent/WTI 2026Q4 forecast reference around $90/$83 and framed risks as two-sided: upside if Middle East supply losses persist, downside if demand weakens further.

assumptions: April 2026 global demand destruction was larger than expected.
Middle East supply losses may prove more persistent.
Demand weakness may deepen or persist.
triggers: More persistent Middle East supply losses would raise upside price risk.
Further evidence of weaker global oil demand would raise downside price risk.
invalidation: A durable de-escalation and rapid normalization of Hormuz flows would reduce upside supply-risk pressure.
A rebound in high-frequency demand indicators would weaken the demand-destruction thesis.
